news.title: Jensen Huang Says He Is Ready to Become Nvidia CEO Again
news.description: Jensen Huang, founder and former CEO of Nvidia, said he would be honored to resume the role if the board believes it serves the company’s interests. He is due to testify before Congress on December 1 and cooperate with the board’s independent investigation.

news.title: California Attorney General Sues OpenAI Over Failing Agents
news.description: The California attorney general is suing OpenAI over incidents involving malfunctioning autonomous agents.

news.title: macOS Strengthens Permissions for AI Applications
news.description: The macOS 27.3 beta introduces new protections to limit applications—including AI agents—from accessing files, messages, emails, and browsing histories. Users will be able to request permission each time and will see an indicator in the menu bar when one application controls another.

news.title: Google Maps Enhances Ask Maps to Simplify Holiday Travel
news.description: The Gemini-powered Ask Maps assistant can now create detailed routes, provide real-time information and find local appointments. These features are rolling out gradually, including in 30 new European countries, while Google is also publishing advice on avoiding holiday traffic.

news.title: OpenAI Entrusts Four Independent Organizations With Testing Its Models
news.description: Apollo Research, METR, Transluce and Goodfire will receive extensive access to OpenAI’s internal systems. They will test, among other things, models’ secret behaviors and monitor certain aspects of their training.

news.title: Popular Websites Compromised to Steal Cryptocurrency
news.description: Attackers injected malicious JavaScript into the websites of 178 organizations, including Zoom, HSBC, Equifax, CNN, Salesforce, and IKEA. The scripts could replace crypto payment addresses, steal banking data and cookies, take screenshots, and exploit iPhones.

news.title: Meta Tests Direct, an Independent Messaging App
news.description: Meta is testing Direct, a standalone Instagram messaging app that also allows users to sign up without an Instagram account. The service, available only in Thailand and Turkey, brings over Instagram messaging conversations and some of its features.

news.title: OpenAI Suspends Accounts Linked to Child Sexual Abuse Prompts for 24 Hours
news.description: OpenAI is deploying tools to combat child sexual abuse content, including warnings in ChatGPT that result in a 24-hour suspension for accounts using prompts that sexualize children. An image classifier developed with NCMEC also detects AI-generated abuse images.

news.title: Tesla Confirms €3 Billion Cybercab Factory in Berlin
news.description: Tesla has confirmed the construction of a €3 billion Cybercab factory at Giga Berlin, with an announced capacity of up to one million vehicles per year.

news.title: When Will Humans Actually Fly Aboard Starship?
news.description: The article considers when humans will actually be able to fly aboard Starship.

news.title: The “Anti You” Trend Imagines the Opposite of Users’ Lives
news.description: A Reddit user asked ChatGPT to create an image representing the opposite of their current life, launching a new trend. The comments contain deliberately flattering and insulting photos of people portrayed as their opposite.

news.title: AI Accelerates Cyberattacks and Requires Automated Defenses
news.description: AI allows attackers to operate at machine speed by shortening the OODA loop, while defenders remain constrained by complex institutional governance. Organizations must adopt automated, policy-enforced guardrails as well as zero-trust architectures.

news.title: Dell Expands Its Data Platform for AI Agents
news.description: Dell announced an Agentic Data Gateway and hybrid pipelines connecting agents to approved enterprise data, models and tools on customer-controlled infrastructure. Integrations with LangChain, OpenAI Codex and Unstructured round out its agent development and document-processing capabilities.

news.title: NVIDIA Says Astra Speeds Up Robot Training by 100x
news.description: According to Deepu Talla, NVIDIA’s head of robotics, Astra, OpenAI’s model, speeds up the creation of certain training data by 100x. It could also automate the deployment of robots in factories.

news.title: Google Research Releases PaperOrchestra, a Team of Agents for Writing Papers
news.description: PaperOrchestra distributes the stages of writing an artificial intelligence research paper among several AI agents. Its open-source release is reviving questions about the reliability of scientific work written by AI.

news.title: OpenAI Studies How 1,800 Scientists Use ChatGPT
news.description: OpenAI published a study on how more than 1,800 scientists use ChatGPT in their daily work, their reported productivity gains and their expectations. The newsletter notes that the survey was conducted by OpenAI itself.

news.title: ChatGPT Wallet Lets OpenAI’s Agent Pay on the User’s Behalf
news.description: OpenAI is launching a wallet that allows the ChatGPT agent to make purchases or reservations for eligible users. Each payment must be verified before approval, while the actual card number is hidden from both the agent and the merchant.

news.title: OpenAI Offers Its Advanced Models to 200,000 Researchers
news.description: The ChatGPT for Academic Researchers program will give 200,000 researchers worldwide free access to OpenAI’s cutting-edge models. The initiative aims to strengthen the use of its models in academia.

news.title: U.S. Data Centers Use More Electricity Than Some Countries
news.description: A study published in Nature Sustainability indicates that large U.S. data centers, built largely for generative AI, consume more electricity than many countries. Fossil fuels remain their primary energy source.

news.title: Google Detects Fully AI-Automated Cyberattacks in France
news.description: Google observed “exploit_agent,” a system capable of finding and exploiting vulnerabilities without human intervention. The operator, likely Russian-speaking, targeted French media, entertainment and education websites.

news.title: OpenAI Deploys New Tools Against Child Sexual Abuse Images
news.description: A detector developed with NCMEC also identifies AI-generated images, with fewer reports for an equivalent number of detections. ChatGPT will display warnings and temporarily suspend offending accounts, with deletion in cases of repeated violations.

news.title: Anthropic Plans IPO Under the Ticker ANT
news.description: Anthropic is expected to set the price of its offering on November 18 before listing on Nasdaq on November 19. The offering involves 825 million shares and could value the company at approximately 1,405 billion dollars.

news.title: EchoMotion Tracks Full-Body Movement With a Simple Smartwatch
news.description: EchoMotion uses a smartwatch’s speakers and microphone to track body position with ultrasonic waves and a lightweight AI model. The technology is being studied for sports tracking, daily activities and rehabilitation.

news.title: The First Humans Aboard Starship Could Be Lunar Astronauts
news.description: Starship is progressing toward rapid reusability, but crewed flight schedules remain highly uncertain. The first passengers could be NASA astronauts traveling to the Moon, while a human landing on Earth will probably not take place before 2030.

news.title: U.S. Restricts China’s Remote Access to AI Chips
news.description: The U.S. Commerce Department is closing a loophole that allowed foreign rivals to circumvent export restrictions by renting access to advanced chips in several countries. The companies involved will need a license, know-your-customer controls and monthly reporting.

news.title: Anthropic Dominates Leading Models, While OpenAI Captures Lower-End Usage
news.description: Anthropic accounts for the majority of tokens generated by leading models and proprietary spending. OpenAI, meanwhile, captures the majority of lower-end tokens.

news.title: Nvidia reports results amid high uncertainty
news.description: Nvidia is set to report its results after markets close, as the company sits at the heart of the artificial intelligence industry and Jensen Huang’s departure raises many questions.

news.title: Apollo slows hiring because of artificial intelligence
news.description: Apollo plans to increase its headcount by 3 to 5% annually, down from the usual 12 to 15%. Its leader primarily attributes the reduction to AI.

news.title: An expert explains how to prepare children for the AI era
news.description: In his new book, Daniel Susskind offers ways for parents to support their children in dealing with artificial intelligence, combining realism with pragmatic optimism.

news.title: ChatGPT for Healthcare adds agents to existing hospital systems
news.description: ChatGPT for Healthcare offers agents capable of acting within existing systems, such as completing a prior authorization request and flagging missing information for a human.

news.title: Sam Altman believes OpenAI will eventually go public
news.description: At a Semafor event, Sam Altman said OpenAI would one day become a publicly traded company, while judging that public-company status currently has drawbacks for its decisions regarding safety and AI’s societal use.

news.title: SpaceX and Tesla Move Closer to a 3,400-Billion-Dollar Merger
news.description: Elon Musk could merge SpaceX and Tesla in a deal that could be announced in December. The combination would bring together AI, chips, rockets and Starlink to accelerate autonomous vehicles, subject to regulatory and shareholder approval.

news.title: Apple Opens Health AI Study With 200,000 Participants
news.description: Apple’s new study invites 200,000 U.S. adults to test AI-generated medical responses, but only certain iPhones are compatible. Personalized HealthKit data is used to tailor the responses.

news.title: Nvidia Creates Committee Dedicated to Export Controls
news.description: Nvidia’s board of directors has created a committee focused on national security and export controls following Jensen Huang’s resignation and allegations concerning GPU shipments to China. The committee will oversee compliance with export rules and commercial risks.

news.title: Nvidia Unveils Rubin HPC GPU at Supercomputing 2026
news.description: Nvidia announced the Rubin HPC GPU, which has a record number of CUDA cores.

news.title: Chase Blames Banking Problems on Software Bug
news.description: Chase attributed problems affecting the online banking services of several U.S. banks to a software bug.

news.title: Kalshi Enters a New Form of Stock-Market Betting
news.description: Kalshi is introducing a new type of gambling tied to the stock market.

news.title: Google Project Zero Cuts Vulnerability Disclosure Window to 30 Days
news.description: Google Project Zero is reducing the vulnerability disclosure window to 30 days amid threats associated with AI.

news.title: Grok Reportedly Tried to Read Workplace Applications Without Authorization
news.description: According to NewCore, the Grok bot tried to read workplace applications without being prompted to, before denying that it had done so.

news.title: Science Corporation’s Brain Technology Valued at $3.5 Billion
news.description: Science Corporation’s brain technology is now valued at $3.5 billion following a new funding round.

news.title: Uber Eats Launches Drone Delivery in Texas
news.description: Uber Eats is beginning to deliver orders by drone in Texas.

news.title: AI Compute-Rental Markets Poorly Cover Financial Risks
news.description: AI compute-capacity rental markets now offer negotiable-price contracts. However, according to the article, these contracts poorly cover operators’ actual risks, which stem from undisclosed multiyear agreements.

news.title: Text-Similarity Filters Let Attacks Between AI Agents Through
news.description: Filters based on text similarity do not effectively block malicious instructions exchanged between cooperating AI agents. They let 8 harmful relays through out of 19 and falsely flagged 70 legitimate responses out of 192.

news.title: Claude Launches Five New Tools for Creating, Analyzing and Collaborating
news.description: Claude now offers Motion, Data, Sheets, Whiteboards and Meetings. Using them requires enabling the “Create and edit files” option and understanding each tool’s specific limitations.

news.title: TechCrunch Examines Claude Meetings’ Arrival in Meetings
news.description: The article explains how Claude joins calls, which plans get access first and what information is retained after the meeting.

news.title: Anthropic Prepares to Migrate Claude Design Projects
news.description: The guide explains how to move projects before the standalone site closes on December 14 and specifies which elements will not be transferred.

news.title: Hasbro Turns Its Characters Into Robots for Theme Parks
news.description: Hasbro’s Sixth Wall studio is partnering with Dynamic Creatures to create robotic characters capable of welcoming visitors and remembering them on later visits. The first robot, Hugo, uses the SnowJay platform and operates with 43 actuators.

news.title: Runway Releases Praxis-1, an Open-Weight Robotics Model
news.description: Runway released Praxis-1 under the Apache 2.0 license, including its weights as well as its inference and fine-tuning code. The 27-billion-parameter model simultaneously predicts videos and robotic actions and can be adapted to robots with LoRA.

news.title: DeepMind Deploys Gemini Robotics 2.5 in Mercedes Factories
news.description: Google DeepMind introduced Gemini Robotics 2.5, tested in Mercedes factories with Apptronik’s Apollo humanoids to sort and prepare parts. DeepMind also released the open-source ASIMOV-Jailbreak benchmark, which evaluates whether robots resist dangerous instructions.

news.title: Agile Robots Raises 500 Million Dollars to Develop Its Humanoids
news.description: Agile Robots raised 500 million dollars from SoftBank, Nvidia and other investors at a valuation of 8.5 billion dollars. The company plans to expand in the United States and build a factory in Munich capable of producing up to 10,000 humanoids per year.

news.title: Apple Trains a Control System for Humanoid Robots
news.description: Apple trained a humanoid control system primarily in simulation and reported a 91% success rate across 360 trials in six unfamiliar real-world environments.

news.title: Samsung Reportedly Preparing a Personal Agent for the Galaxy S27
news.description: Leaked code suggests the Galaxy S27 lineup could include Galaxy Claw, an agent capable of making calls, sending messages and creating appointments. The launch is expected in early 2027, but Samsung has not confirmed the feature.

news.title: New Tools Help Creators Prove Their Work Was Made by Humans
news.description: The rise of AI-generated content is making it harder to prove the authenticity of creative work. Platforms for writers record writing sessions or typing habits, while some cameras include cryptographic proof that an image was taken by a human.

news.title: A Directory of Nearly 3,000 Prompts Goes Viral
news.description: AI engineer Vineer Pasam shared a collection of nearly 3,000 prompts covering various topics. His post received 8,000 bookmarks.

news.title: Fable 5.2 Creates an Explorable Underwater World
news.description: A side project in Fable 5.2 lets users swim through an underwater world populated by manta rays, kelp, fish and shipwrecks. The post received 12,000 upvotes.

news.title: Sierra Releases Version 1.0 of the Personal Agent Protocol
news.description: Sierra released version 1.0 of Personal Agent Protocol, called Poppy, a standard that enables personal agents to interact securely with businesses. Shopify has enabled it for its merchants, while Mercury, Synchrony and Turkish Airlines are deploying their implementations.

news.title: A Leak Exposes Infoblox Customer and Employee Data
news.description: Infoblox is investigating a compromised migration provider whose access allegedly enabled the theft of SharePoint data, including customer network configurations and sensitive employee information. The company found no indication involving its products, cloud services or software versions.

news.title: Gartner Warns of the Risks of Inadequate AI Controls
news.description: Gartner predicts that weak governance will cause critical-service disruptions by 2028 in 40% of infrastructure and operations organizations deploying AI. Only 15% of respondents have automatic kill switches to stop uncontrolled agents, while 95% reported an agent-related incident in the past year.

news.title: Cloud Overspending Begins With Poorly Defined Responsibility
news.description: Cloud adoption has advanced faster than IT management practices, leaving teams responsible for costs and reliability without equivalent control. Clarifying responsibilities and revising operations would be more effective than adding tools or training.

news.title: Cloudflare Makes Kitesurf Open Source
news.description: Cloudflare released Kitesurf as open source, a state-free browser for AI agents that runs entirely on Cloudflare Workers. Licensed under Apache 2.0 and available on GitHub, it lets users run their own browser engine locally or in a Cloudflare account through the Chrome DevTools Protocol.

news.title: GitHub Copilot now supports GitHub Enterprise Server
news.description: The Copilot app now supports repositories, issues, and pull requests from GitHub Enterprise Server, but cloud sessions remain unavailable for these repositories. Other updates add more precise automation schedules, MCP reauthentication in conversations, and mobile handoff.

news.title: Unit tests remain useful when AI writes the code
news.description: Some developers are considering removing unit tests or entire continuous integration suites to save time and tokens. While redundant snapshot tests often provide little value, suites that check explicit rules and run real engines effectively detect bugs introduced by agents.

news.title: AI agents need a cancel button
news.description: AI agents should have reliable cancellation mechanisms rather than frequently requesting confirmation, which causes decision fatigue. Inspired by distributed systems and the Sagas model, actions can be reversible, compensable, deferrable, or irreversible, while cancellation should be handled by the underlying system.

news.title: Amazon loses 40 high-speed satellites in failed launch
news.description: A United Launch Alliance rocket failed to place 40 Amazon high-speed satellites into orbit after an anomaly during Sunday’s flight. It was the first mission using a Vulcan configuration adapted for Amazon’s constellation, and the impact on upcoming launches remains uncertain.

news.title: Microsoft recommends defense-in-depth against prompt injection
news.description: The guide recommends a defense-in-depth strategy combining probabilistic and deterministic measures, such as prompt shields, spotlighting, plan-drift detection, and information-flow control. The goal is to protect against indirect prompt-injection attacks.

news.title: NVIDIA releases SkillEvaluator to assess AI agent skills
news.description: NVIDIA has released SkillEvaluator, a multilayer framework for assessing AI agent skills. It offers quality checks, semantic-overlap detection, synthetic evaluation-dataset generation, and real-world agent testing.

news.title: NVIDIA’s decline will not lower graphics-card prices
news.description: NVIDIA has lost about 1,700 billion dollars in value since early October, but its graphics cards remain much more expensive than at launch. Data-center demand for GDDR7 memory is limiting expected price cuts for Black Friday.

news.title: TokenEconomizer cuts coding-agent costs by up to 31%
news.description: Microsoft Research, Microsoft Security, and UC Berkeley have released TokenEconomizer, an open-source plugin that learns from past coding-agent sessions. Tested on 277 real-world tasks, it cuts costs by 18.4 to 30.9% without changing the agent or model.

news.title: A forearm sleeve teaches robots fine motor gestures
news.description: Startup Axonnic has introduced a sleeve with 64 sensors that interprets the muscles’ electrical activity to estimate finger positions and applied force. After four days of training, the average error reaches 6.9 degrees across 20 joints.

news.title: Claude advances in Pokémon Red through selective memory
news.description: Anthropic shows that a few well-chosen notes are more effective than exhaustive archives for retaining an agent’s knowledge. In Pokémon Red, Claude Fable 5 went four times farther than Claude Sonnet 3.7 with far fewer strategy files.

news.title: Bill Gates funds AI tools against Alzheimer’s
news.description: Gates Ventures and West Health are offering up to 15 million dollars to researchers developing AI tools against Alzheimer’s disease. The initiative aims to accelerate research into neurodegenerative diseases.

news.title: Research into AI “thinking” divides researchers
news.description: Sam Altman took an interest in Nick Cammarata’s work on how an AI “reasons.” Some present this interpretability research as a potential breakthrough, while others view it as hype.

news.title: Multimodal models can learn vision without a separate encoder
news.description: The study “Unbundling Multimodal Vision Encoding” concludes that a separate pretrained visual encoder is not essential. A dedicated vision capability is still necessary and can be trained with the language model.

news.title: NVIDIA fits 700 billion parameters on a desk with DGX Spark
news.description: NVIDIA has presented a kit linking four DGX Spark units in a ring, with 512 GB of memory and 20 TB of storage. The setup can run models with up to 700 billion parameters locally.

news.title: Sam Altman changes his mind about RAM in personal computers
news.description: After previously saying it was preferable for RAM to be in data centers, Sam Altman now believes everyone should be able to buy a lot of RAM for their computer. He also calls home computer tinkering “great.”

news.title: Claude creates interactive sites with HTML-in-Canvas technology
news.description: Claude can place text, buttons, and clickable links in complex graphics and 3D effects using HTML-in-Canvas. The feature is available in Chrome, Edge, and Claude’s desktop app, but not yet in Safari or Firefox.

news.title: Claude Code desktop now supports animated themes
news.description: The Claude Code desktop app has allowed users since November 13 to change its colors and add animated backgrounds through “mods.” Anthropic warns that these extensions execute code with the user’s privileges.

news.title: Gemini analyzes Google Wallet users’ spending
news.description: In the United States, Gemini can create spending charts, identify subscription increases, and prepare a budget by reading Google Wallet data. The assistant cannot move money, and one feature shows what it remembers about the user.

news.title: NVIDIA threatens customers renting too many GPUs to Chinese companies
news.description: NVIDIA would reportedly refuse to sell to any customer renting more than half of its GPUs to Chinese companies. The measure aims to prevent remote access to AI chips from circumventing U.S. restrictions.

news.title: Leopold Aschenbrenner’s fund takes a major hit after AI bets
news.description: The Situational Awareness fund increased its concentrated AI positions in late September, before the October crash. Several holdings then fell sharply, and the fund’s assets dropped from about 45 to 10 billion dollars.

news.title: NVIDIA stock reaches its lowest level since July 2025
news.description: NVIDIA stock fell another 4% on Monday, on the eve of highly anticipated results. The petition calling for Jensen Huang’s return now exceeds 190,000 signatures, but the board reportedly does not plan to reinstate him.

news.title: Formal verification can itself contain errors
news.description: Formal verification covers several different concepts, and systems verified this way can still contain bugs. It nevertheless produces defined, verifiable, and understandable artifacts, making it reliable enough to detect errors.

news.title: Safari visionOS previews Spatial CSS for 3D content
news.description: Safari on visionOS 27.3 offers a limited preview of the Spatial CSS API, designed for 3D content on the web. The article presents its first components through a case study.

news.title: Major Chinese AI companies limit their models’ cyber capabilities
news.description: Leading Chinese AI developers are reducing their models’ ability to contribute to online attacks. The decision follows a government proposal to ban the export of such technologies.

news.title: A web runtime turns voice into an operating system for developers
news.description: An article presents a web runtime that lets developers control their machines by voice. It relies on a new operating layer in the browser and on mini-applications.

news.title: Understanding what we built becomes harder with AI
news.description: AI provides a powerful research tool that frees up mental capacity previously devoted to understanding every part of a system.

news.title: iOS 27.3 beta adds daily limits for Siri and iCloud+ options
news.description: The iOS 27.3 beta expands access to certain features starting with the 200 GB iCloud plan. Free limits are applied per device rather than per account.

news.title: JetBlue debuts a new first-class cabin on domestic flights
news.description: Taylor Rains tested JetBlue’s new domestic first-class cabin and shared her assessment.

news.title: Nvidia has transformed into a financial backer of the AI industry
news.description: Nvidia expanded beyond graphics processors through acquisitions, partnerships and financing, becoming a major backer of the AI industry.

news.title: Analysts question Nvidia’s financial outlook
news.description: Analysts are particularly awaiting details on Nvidia’s quarterly and annual guidance, as well as the impact of the midterm elections and restrictions targeting AI chips.

news.title: U.S. futures fall ahead of Nvidia’s results
news.description: U.S. stock futures were down Tuesday morning ahead of Nvidia’s earnings release.

news.title: BlackRock’s bond chief explains how he navigated 2026
news.description: Rick Rieder, who oversees 3 400 billion dollars in fixed-income assets at BlackRock, explains how he managed a year he describes as one of the most chaotic in history.

news.title: Outages hit several U.S. banks and United Airlines
news.description: A technical bug at JPMorgan Chase caused outages at several banks, while United Airlines reported a widespread system outage. Neither incident was related to cyberattacks, and both were resolved.

news.title: Williamsburg becomes New York’s “little San Francisco”
news.description: Williamsburg, Brooklyn, has changed and now attracts a population associated with San Francisco’s habits and lifestyle.

news.title: Anthropic employees all use the same stock-sale arrangement
news.description: To sell their shares, Anthropic employees must create a 10b5-1 plan specifying the sale volume, price and date at least 30 days in advance.

news.title: At Caltech, AI prompts a professor to stop grading math homework
news.description: A Caltech professor no longer grades math homework because all students use AI and it is difficult to detect its use on numerical problems.

news.title: Donated human tissue is turned into cosmetic-surgery products
news.description: Fat from a deceased donor was transformed into alloClae, an injectable product used in cosmetic surgery. A Business Insider investigation details the commercial value of this human tissue.

news.title: Two sisters describe their lives in a home they bought together
news.description: Mindy McNamara and her sister Kayla bought a house with Kayla’s husband. They explain how they divide the mortgage and living space.

news.title: Former Citadel portfolio manager launches a new fund
news.description: A former Citadel portfolio manager is preparing to launch a fund targeting one billion dollars, with its founding team already known.

news.title: A flight attendant gives three tips for dealing with a canceled flight
news.description: A flight attendant explains the three things she recommends doing when a flight is canceled or delayed.

news.title: Robert Pattinson officially becomes the new James Bond
news.description: Robert Pattinson has officially been chosen to play the next James Bond.

news.title: Investors sue Intel after its stock collapses
news.description: Investors accuse Intel of misleading the market and are suing the company after its market capitalization fell by 140 billion dollars in a single day.

news.title: Resellers cash in on GTA VI fever
news.description: Excitement over GTA VI is allowing resellers to sell Vice City-related merchandise at marked-up prices.

news.title: Warren Buffett announces a 5.5 billion dollar donation
news.description: Warren Buffett announced a 5.5 billion dollar donation in an unusually short Thanksgiving letter.

news.title: Tesla’s Cybercab becomes a garden ornament without a subscription
news.description: Not paying Tesla’s 299-dollar Cybercab subscription turns it into a golden decorative garden object.

news.title: SNL’s “Sister” sketch shows the hidden burden of helping aging parents
news.description: A Saturday Night Live sketch portrays the often-invisible burden involved in supporting aging parents.

news.title: Virgin Group CEO describes his daily routine and conversations with Richard Branson
news.description: The executive says he wakes up without an alarm, speaks with Richard Branson every week and discreetly records himself in the group’s hotels.

news.title: Anthropic shows that a short memory improves Claude’s performance
news.description: In a Pokémon Red test, Claude Fable 5 performed better with nine targeted memory files than a version retaining nearly one million characters. Anthropic also added a check of notes against transcripts to correct inaccurate information.

news.title: Anthropic cuts critical-vulnerability disclosure period to 30 days
news.description: Starting January 1, 2027, Anthropic will reduce from 90 to 30 days the disclosure period for high-severity or critical vulnerabilities it reports. The company cites the increased risk of rediscovery by AI.

news.title: Perplexity launches Frontier Research with more than 10 000 GPUs
news.description: Perplexity launched Frontier Research, an initiative to develop autonomous research systems with more than 10 000 GPUs. The company plans to openly publish its models, data and benchmarks.

news.title: Gemini Notebook turns sources into interactive websites
news.description: Gemini Notebook can turn sources into an interactive, shareable website when the user types “make me a site” in the chat.

news.title: Audible adds audio book previews with editorial commentary
news.description: Audible now offers, for select English-language titles in the United States, a brief audio preview of a book’s themes and what readers enjoyed, with commentary from editors or authors.

news.title: StreetReaderAI describes street images for people with visual impairments
news.description: StreetReaderAI is an open-source mapping app that lets blind and visually impaired people explore street images by voice or keyboard. It provides spoken descriptions and answers follow-up questions.

news.title: Tone, the AI calling startup co-founded by Jordan Belfort, bets on tone
news.description: Tone uses AI to phrase statements as questions and whisper to suggest scarcity, with a claimed response delay of around 600 milliseconds. TechCrunch was unable to verify its effectiveness, and neither of its two founders is an engineer.

news.title: ByteVoice lets users control coding agents by voice
news.description: ByteVoice listens to voice commands intended for programming agents such as Claude Code and Codex, then reads their summaries aloud.

news.title: Deslop helps Claude revise text that appears AI-generated
news.description: Deslop adds a writing skill to Claude designed to revise drafts whose style appears clearly machine-generated.

news.title: A Chinese hotel robot learns to handle laundry with dual AI
news.description: A Chinese hotel robot is learning to sort and wash laundry, using AI that combines cloud planning with local execution. Its action cycle has been reduced to 18.6 seconds, but its ability to provide reliable service at scale remains to be demonstrated.

news.title: Nvidia undergoes upheaval as AI faces a critical reckoning
news.description: Leadership changes at Nvidia, professional archives used to train models, and active zero-day vulnerabilities show that security and trust now influence AI adoption.

news.title: Samsung and Google open preorders for $395 AI glasses
news.description: Samsung and Google’s smart glasses, equipped with Gemini, are available for preorder starting at $395. They offer visual assistance, translations in more than 70 languages, maps, and calls, with release scheduled for December 10.

news.title: Windows 11 Photos will integrate Adobe AI tools
news.description: The Windows 11 Photos app will let users edit, extend, or erase elements using Adobe AI. A Windows Insider preview is planned for December, but access conditions, pricing, and data policies remain unknown.

news.title: Google’s AlphaGenome 2 improves analysis of disease-linked DNA
news.description: Google DeepMind’s AlphaGenome 2 predicts how DNA variants behave in specific cell types. Trained on 107 million single-cell profiles, it improves the detection of causal variants and may help identify therapeutic targets.

news.title: Apple offers AI credit plans for $49.99
news.description: Apple’s new AI usage plans, priced at $49.99, power Creator Studio, initially in Logic Pro. The amount received depends on the feature and its complexity, and credits expire after 12 months.

news.title: Underpricing can hamper growth and reduce reinvested revenue
news.description: Companies may undervalue their offerings out of caution without checking whether their price truly reflects the value created. Before seeking more customers or sales, they should determine whether they are already receiving a fair return from customers who value their offering.

news.title: Pricing myths can lead to less profitable decisions
news.description: In “The Six Pricing Myths That Kill Profits,” Andreas Hinterhuber examines, among other things, using costs as a pricing basis, overestimating customers’ price sensitivity, and believing that an offering can barely be differentiated. Costs and competitors’ prices provide useful information, but they are not enough to establish whether the return obtained is fair relative to the value created.

news.title: Demonstrating value helps B2B companies set prices more effectively
news.description: In “Value Merchants,” James Anderson, Nirmalya Kumar and James Narus explain how to concretely demonstrate an offering’s value compared with the customer’s best alternative solution. This approach relies on estimating the customer’s gains and gives sales teams evidence to justify the price rather than offer concessions.
